source_contracts.trace: OutfitOutcome represents an ordered successful garment prefix, human warnings about successful garments, an optional stopping error, and checkpoints for every attempted garment. The current attempt checkpoint is appended before result matching. Success extends prefix; first failure returns that prefix plus error and its checkpoint; all-success returns no error. These outputs intentionally coexist, so replacing them with one success/failure payload that discards partial geometry or checkpoints would lose supported behavior. DrapeOutcome remains one attempt result/warnings/checkpoints as already traced780/782.

source_contracts.trace: Some(saved) calls SettledDrape.wear(&input), which produces the same single-attempt DrapeOutcome contract as live drape(input, previous.get(index), cancel,...). Source-accounted saved owner78849-308 distinguishes bound saved cloth/body correspondence from live mutable fit state; input ownership and actual same input feed both paths. Saved success preview and live stage preview each append the current garment to the completed prefix. Saved/live representations should not be flattened or implemented as duplicate identity/geometry authorities.

source_contracts.role: Preview snapshots versus committed successful garments
source_contracts.trace: Preview owns a cloned prefix plus current available garment; finished is extended only after Ok result. A preview during a failed live attempt may have included transient current geometry; returned final garments contain only the successful prefix. Both use Vec<DrapedGarment> because payload shape matches; named callback/output boundaries distinguish lifecycle without an evidenced need for a public parallel garment wrapper.

source_contracts.role: Human diagnostic text versus machine state
source_contracts.trace: Warnings name their garment through formatted human text. problems collects these and prepends contextual formatted anyhow error, returning None when there is no problem text. Free-form human diagnostics and open underlying error causes are distinct from the machine stopping predicate/error Option; no closed magic-string status enum or duplicate warning/error owner is justified by actual use. Outcome.problem wording is presentation, not parsed identity or authoritative garment matching.

source_contracts.role: Actual asynchronous receiver and retained checkpoint ownership
source_contracts.trace: DrapeWorker pending Vec<(T,DrapeInput)> is unzipped once into draping tags and corresponding inputs, then those inputs and taken previous checkpoints are moved into the single spawned drape_outfit call. The preview callback stores matching prefix snapshots only while uncancelled. Join receives OutfitOutcome (or an explicit thread-failure outcome); poll takes outcome.checkpoints into worker state even for failed/cancelled completion, then publishes successful-prefix preview/finished only when uncancelled. Thus the published outcome has had its checkpoint vector taken: do not claim every downstream finished record retains all checkpoints. The machine event fields may coexist in one poll; no unsupported single worker-state enum redesign inferred.

source_contracts.role: Native cancellation predicate and optional collections
source_contracts.trace: AtomicBool is the actual shared thread-cancellation primitive consumed by live drape/preview/worker. Empty input validly returns an empty successful outfit. Option on saved state, prior slot, diagnostics and stopping error expresses actual absence at distinct boundaries, not duplicate Boolean flags needing arbitrary bounds. No cancellation, concurrency or fresh-versus-cached behavior correctness claim transferred from the role assessment.
